messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-23456 -> inference-hotpath-queue backlog > 90% (15m). source: autoscaler-controller. Details: https://pd.local/PD-23456 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-23456 — page sent to schedule 'eng-oncall' (auto-escalation in 5m).

sanjay: Ack'd. I'm on it. Starting triage — checking autoscaler logs and cloud provisioning.

kate-engops: I see node provision requests stuck in cloud API queue, lots of 429s from provider. Possibly control-plane throttle. Confirming region is us-west-2c.

mike-sre: tl;dr: autoscaler is healthy but provider returning RATE_LIMIT on instance create. Backlog growing while kube-scheduler is holding pods.

sanjay: Running quick mitigation: switching a portion of pool to on-demand to bypass spot depletion. Command: `kubectl label nodepool hotpath temporary-on-demand=true` then trigger rollout.

alice-product: any customer impact? Threads from support show increased latency for streaming completions, some timeouts. Not yet a widespread failure but several major customers reported degraded tail latency.

sanjay: Timeline: backlog ramped at 02:13, PD page at 02:18. Estimated queued tokens ~1.2M, queue depth 8600 requests.

kate-engops: Executed on-demand rotation, but cloud API still returning 429 for some requests. Opening a support case with provider.

sanjay: As fallback I'm going to temporarily increase replica target for inference-deployment to soak existing nodes (risk higher CPU) so in-flight requests drain. `kubectl scale deploy/inference-deployment --replicas=50` then pin model to smaller-variant to reduce memory pressure.

mike-sre: Deploy-bot finished scaling, new replicas scheduled but Pending due to node shortage. Need to force-create nodes via provider console as manual override.

kate-engops: Manual node create succeeded (3 on-demand). Nodes registered at 02:33, kubelet joined. Starting pod scheduling.

sanjay: Queue depth falling: 8600 -> 4200 -> 900 over 18 minutes. Good signal. Switching autoscaler back to normal after stabilization.

pagerduty: PD-23456 acknowledged by sanjay at 02:35.

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler-controller logs show repeated `CreateInstance 429` errors from cloud-provider between 02:10–02:30. Recommendation: consider exponential backoff jitter and fallback to on-demand pool in controller.

alice-product: Customer comms: I've drafted a short note for affected customers: slow tail latencies during 02:10–02:40 PST, mitigation in progress, engineers are investigating root cause.

mike-sre: Followups: 1) add fallback to on-demand when provider 429 rate > X 2) surface provider-rate metrics in console 3) run a chaos test to simulate provider throttles.

sanjay: Agree. I'll open a ticket to update autoscaler strategy and add a 'throttle-detection' alert with playbook.

oncall-replacement: Handing off to morning oncall — cluster stabilized, queue drained to normal levels. I will monitor for next 2 hours then close PD.

incident-bot: PD-23456 -> resolved (manual mitigation + on-demand nodes) at 02:52. Please file postmortem if followups required. :white_check_mark:

alice-product: Filing customer follow-up and postmortem request. Thanks all.

mike-sre: Adding runbook note: when provider 429s spike, send immediate page to eng-oncall AND ops to perform on-demand rotation (runbook id: RB-043).

sanjay: Created GH issue: redwood/autoscaler#478 - provider-rate-limit fallback + dashboard.

kate-engops: Provider support responded: they throttled due to regional capacity pressure; they recommended spreading instance requests across AZs and using smaller-batch API calls.

incident-bot: Thread closed by oncall at 03:00.
